# BASELINES — head-to-head GPU race-detector comparison

_Generated by `eval/baselines/make_tables.py` from `eval/results/baselines-*.csv`. Facts only._

**Environment (actual):** SLURM cluster; runs on RTX 4060 Ti (sm_89, partition rtx4060ti16g) with RTX 3060 Ti (sm_86) for the sm_86 spot checks; CUDA 13.3 toolkit (`/usr/local/cuda`), driver 580.82.07, Compute Sanitizer 2026.2.1.0, NVBit 1.8, GNU Make 4.2.1, networkx 3.6.1, `.env/bin/python` = CPython 3.14. NOTE: the task brief specified RTX A5000 / driver 595 / CUDA 12.9; toolkit/driver differ and are recorded here.

| B2 HiRace | BUILT / RUN on the whole Indigo original suite | **Correction:** the earlier record ("the artifact ships only the 21 nobug base patterns instrumented") was a **harness bug**: `run_hirace.py` globbed `*/*_hirace.cu`, which matches only the 21 base files; the SC24 artifact in fact ships **590** hand-instrumented sources (`indigo/indigo_hirace_sources/<pattern>/<pattern>_hirace<bug-suffix>.cu`), bug variants included. Those 21-pattern rows are superseded (kept in `eval/results/superseded_hirace_21/`; old runner in `setup/run_hirace.21patterns.py.superseded`). HiRace is a header-only source-level runtime (`src/hirace/*.h`, plain `nvcc -DRACECHECK -I src/hirace`). It now runs on every row of **PI** (all 590 IndigoSuite codes × 7 inputs) with that row's graph and launch, slowdown vs the uninstrumented build of the same code. The artifact's own `make table1` is also run verbatim (`setup/p_hirace_table1.sh`; only accommodations: a symlink for its hard-coded iGUARD detector path to our NVBit-1.8 build, and an isolated venv `setup/tools/hirace_venv` for the `matplotlib`/`tabulate` imports of its scripts) and reported next to the paper's Table I. **Instrumenter / portability:** Table 1 does not use an instrumenter (the driver says *"manually created hirace files, pairing them up until automatic instrumentation is done"*). `src/clang` (CudaRW) is an unfinished libTooling prototype: it rewrites only kernel parameters literally named `data1`/`data2`, emits an API (`data_ptr`, `setMetadata`) that the shipped runtime (`HIRACE_WRAP_DATA` macros) does not have, does no host-side work (shadow allocation, launch arguments), and its CMake (`add_clang_executable`) builds only inside an LLVM source tree (no clang/LLVM on this cluster). So HiRace cannot be applied automatically to any other CUDA code. It *can* be applied by hand (wrap each device array with the macros, add `hr_shadowt*` kernel params, allocate/pass shadow arrays on the host) — the authors did that for six non-Indigo programs in `fig6-tests/` — but hand-editing Indigo3 / ECL / ScoR / cuHadron / HeCBench sources is outside this comparison's rules, so HiRace has no rows there. **`make table1` run conditions (2026-09-20/21):** the unmodified driver was first started on `rtx4060ti16g` node c67, where every iGUARD process idled after finishing until the driver's 300 s timeout and orphans accumulated (the driver kills only the shell); cause not found (static-vs-shared cudart was tested and refuted), job cancelled. It then ran to completion, unmodified, on `rtx4060ti8g` node c26 (job 285364, 6 h 24 min, 590 codes × 6 graphs × {indigo, memcheck+racecheck, iGUARD, HiRace}), with the only accommodation `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` pinned to the node's RTX 4060 Ti (`setup/pin8g.sh`; NVBit fails when the node's second, older GPU is visible), the artifact's hard-coded iGUARD path provided as a symlink to our NVBit-1.8 build, and matplotlib/tabulate from `setup/tools/hirace_venv`. Counts only — its timings are from a different CPU and are not used. Result (`eval/results/baselines-hirace-table1.csv`, BASELINES.md §HiRace artifact Table 1): our own HiRace runner agrees with it on 3540/3540 (code, graph) verdicts; on the paper's 346-racy-test basis HiRace reproduces 346/0 on the four ≥100-vertex graphs (paper 346/0), 186/160 on `DAG_5n_5e` (paper 182/164) and 303/43 on `counterDAG_5n_5e` (paper 295/51); the shipped `gen_table1.py` itself uses a 266-test basis (drops all `boundsBug` codes), and its Sequential column is a stub. |
| B3 iGUARD | BUILT / RUN (P1–P6) | The earlier BUILD-BLOCKED record was a **harness bug**: the box ran `make ARCH=89` but iGUARD's Makefile passes `-arch=$(ARCH)` to nvcc, which needs `sm_89` (error was literally `Unsupported gpu architecture '89'`). Real constraint underneath: iGUARD pins NVBit 1.7.4 (driver ≤ 555.xx) while the nodes run driver 580.82.07 / CUDA 13.3, so the detector was built against **NVBit 1.8** (CUDA 13.2 headers, sha256 `72a2b827…`) with `make ARCH=sm_89`; it compiled **unmodified** (`setup/iguard_diffs/` empty). Runner: `LD_PRELOAD=detector.so` (iGUARD README). Gotcha found while validating: NVBit strips `LD_PRELOAD` in the first process it lands in, so the app must not be wrapped in `timeout`/`env` launchers. Scope limits (from `detector.cu`): only `cuMemAlloc`/`cuMemAllocManaged`-tracked memory is checked — `__device__` globals (the canary) and `__shared__` are not; races are attributed to a fence/scope/lock class (`Race: Missing blkfence|gpufence|strong op|lock|warpsync`, `Improper atom scope`). spack (`setup/spack_setup.sh`) provides the README's missing packages (GNU `time`, TBB headers); the detector itself needs neither. |

SuperCollider is a redundant-read pass **inside NVIDIA's proprietary `ptxas`**; the artifact states the modified compiler cannot be distributed, so it ships only pre-instrumented binaries (cuHadron 27 tests racy+fixed, 99 original-Indigo tests, 10 HeCBench apps) plus the runtime `lib64/librc-release.so` (proprietary, Compute Sanitizer SLA; enabled with `CUDA_INJECTION64_PATH`). **Consequence: it cannot be run on P1–P5/P7** (no way to instrument Indigo3, ECL, ScoR or the canary). To still get a like-for-like comparison, the other detectors run the same programs built from the same sources: its 99 Indigo tests are a tagged **subset view of PI** (the whole Indigo original suite; its binaries embed the HiRace SC24 artifact's `indigo_sources` paths, which are those same 590 codes), **P9** = its 10 HeCBench apps with its arguments; cuHadron is our existing P6. Detection is probabilistic; the artifact's own protocol of 5 attempts per program is used (RACE if any attempt reports). Its overhead is measured against the artifact's own uninstrumented binaries in the same container. P9 labels are the paper's racy/race-free flags, not an independent oracle. |

## 1b. Residual ERROR/TIMEOUT root causes (cuVein)

Every program that was ERROR/TIMEOUT in scalar-clock mode (plus all of P7) was re-run by `parallel.py run --timeout-floor 1200` with the native rc/stderr, the accelprof stderr and the raw-dump size captured; `classify_residuals.py` assigns one cause per (program, mode). GPU nodes have 188 GB RAM and a 914 GB node-local scratch disk; peak_mb is the collector's peak RSS in MB.

- **resolved** — verdict obtained with the 20-min cap (was an overhead timeout)
- **app-native-fail** — the program exits non-zero WITHOUT accelprof: app/corpus/args, not the collector
- **trace-volume** — TIMEOUT while the dump kept growing: the access count exceeds the 20-min tracing budget
- **collector-hang** — TIMEOUT with an empty dump and modest RSS: the collector stalled
- **collector-memory** — TIMEOUT with an empty dump but ≥32 GB RSS: the collector holds the whole trace in memory (nothing written before the end): **attributable to the cuVein collector**
- **collector-oom** — native rc 0 but the accelprof child was SIGKILLed (`Killed`): the collector's memory grows with the trace: **attributable to the cuVein collector**
- **hb-clock-hang** — vector-clock-mode TIMEOUT with an empty dump while scalar-clock of the same program resolved: **attributable to cuVein's vector-clock runtime (HbClock)** (not the tracer)
- **collector-fail** — native rc 0 but accelprof rc≠0 / no kernel JSON: **attributable to the cuVein collector**
- **trace-disk-full** — the raw dump filled the node-local scratch disk (`No space left on device`): **attributable to the cuVein collector** (unbounded dump)
- **analysis-oom** — the collector finished but the Python `sync_dominance` analysis of the trace was Killed (OOM): **attributable to cuVein's scalar-clock analysis path**
- **analysis-timeout** — the collector finished (dump size/kernels in the row) but the offline `sync_dominance` analysis exceeded its wall-clock cap (`--analysis-timeout`): **attributable to cuVein's scalar-clock analysis path**

Cells: `RACE(n)` = race reported with n deduped reports; `CLEAN`; `TO` timeout; `ERR`; `—` not run. cuVein-VC = C++ HbClock verdict; cuVein-SC = scalar-clock (sync_dominance static leg). Footnotes: (1) HiRace is source-level and has no usable instrumenter (its `src/clang` prototype only rewrites kernel params named `data1`/`data2`, emits an API the shipped runtime does not have and needs an LLVM source tree to build); it runs only on the 590 IndigoSuite codes its artifact ships hand-instrumented, which are exactly the Indigo original suite. (2) SuperCollider's compiler pass is not distributed; it exists only as pre-instrumented binaries for cuHadron and its own Indigo/HeCBench subsets. (3) iGUARD was not run on the HeCBench overhead set. (4) 16 cuHadron targets need sm_90 and count as ERR for every tool that was pointed at them. (5) Programs without a racy/race-free label are in neither ratio: Indigo original suite 1008, Indigo original suite — SuperCollider's 99-test subset on its own input 10, HeCBench overhead set 14 (HeCBench overhead apps are unlabelled; Indigo `boundsBug` codes are out-of-bounds bugs, excluded by both the HiRace and the SuperCollider artifact's ground truth). (6) HeCBench-subset labels are the SuperCollider paper's racy/race-free flags, not an independent oracle. (7) Two cuHadron categories are out of cuVein's scope (user decision, 2026-09-21); their rows are kept, not excluded, because the labels apply to every detector. `asyncmemcpy/*` races a host-API `cudaMemcpyAsync` against a kernel on another stream: the collector's async-copy tracer covers the in-kernel `cp.async` instruction (the `memcpy/*` tests, which cuVein does run), and the race tool consumes no host memcpy events. `interkernel/*` races two kernels on different streams: the happens-before model is per kernel launch. cuVein verdicts on them: asyncmemcpy vector-clock: CLEAN 2, RACE 2; asyncmemcpy scalar-clock: CLEAN 2, RACE 2; asyncmemcpy collector-only: CLEAN 2, RACE 2; interkernel vector-clock: CLEAN 4; interkernel scalar-clock: CLEAN 4; interkernel collector-only: CLEAN 4 (4 program-inputs per category). Their failures are trace volume of the kernels themselves (`kernel_memcpy_dtoh_race`: 64M threads × 201 writes ≈ 1.3e10 traced accesses; `memcpy_htod_kernel_race`: ≈ 2.6e8 reads, vector-clock mode only; `interkernel/global_writewrite_race`: ≈ 1.1e8 events, finishes only with the 20-minute cap). Not re-run for that reason: the longer-cap diagnose re-runs of `kernel_memcpy_dtoh_race` (cancelled after node failures on c3, c2, c75), the `memcpy_htod_kernel_race-fixed` row lost to a full scratch disk on c37, and the `interkernel/global_writewrite_race-fixed` diagnose task that was OOM-killed on c53. (9) Labelled race-free, reported under the instance gate (T12, D11): PTX section 8.7.1 gives no ordering where one side of a hand-off has no fence of sufficient scope. `P4-reduction-norace-small`: the ticket `atomicInc` is followed by the shared store `amLast` with no fence in between (the program relies on the `__syncthreads()` after it) (also reported by iguard); `P4-reduction-norace-large`: the ticket `atomicInc`, as in the small input (also reported by iguard); `P5-norace_interblock_fence_raw`: the consumer spins on the flag with a relaxed `atomicExch` and has no fence before it reads the volatile data (SC) (no baseline reports it); `P5-norace_interwarp_fence_raw`: the consumer spins on the flag with a relaxed `atomicExch` and has no fence before it reads the volatile data (SC) (no baseline reports it); `P5-norace_interwarp_blkfence_raw`: the consumer spins on the flag with a relaxed `atomicExch` and has no fence before it reads the volatile data (SC) (no baseline reports it); `P5-norace_interwarp-block_fence_hrf-indirect`: the consumer spins on the flag with a relaxed `atomicAdd` and has no fence before it updates the volatile data (SC) (no baseline reports it); `P5-norace_interwarp-block_fence-atom_hrd-indirect`: the consumer spins on the flag with a relaxed `atomicAdd` and has no fence before it does a block-scope `atomicExch` on data the other block writes with a device-scope one (not morally strong: DR) (no baseline reports it). (8) **Are the Indigo-original FNs racy?** The suite labels a CODE racy (a planted `atomicBug`/`guardBug`/`syncBug`), but whether two threads actually conflict depends on the input graph. `oracle_pi/oracle_pi.py` (→ `eval/results/baselines-pi-oracle.csv`) decides it per (code, input) independently of every detector: the unmodified source is compiled for the CPU with an access-logging `data_t`, each GPU thread runs as a fiber with `__syncthreads` barriers and warp collectives emulated, under 3 thread schedules, and a row is CONFLICT iff two different threads touch one location, at least one writes, not both atomic, with no barrier/collective between them (source-level: an elided store still counts). Checked inputs: `DAG_100n_100e`, `DAG_5n_5e`, `counterDAG_5n_5e` (every FN of cuVein and HiRace is on these). Result: 148 of 798 racy-labelled rows have NO conflicting access on their input (e.g. `DAG_5n_5e` has every edge pointing to a lower vertex id, so a `cond` variant's `if (i < nei)` is never true and the buggy update is never reached; with `guardBug` the unguarded write only happens when the compared value is larger, which it never is there; the 4 rows on `DAG_100n_100e` are block-per-vertex codes launched with SuperCollider's 4 blocks, so only vertices 0–3 run and they update two different elements, one thread each); 0 of 540 bug-free rows show a conflict. FN split per detector — cuVein (vector-clock): 148 not racy on the input, 0 real misses; cuVein (scalar-clock): 148 not racy on the input, 0 real misses; cuVein (collector-only): 124 not racy on the input, 1 real misses; compute-sanitizer racecheck: 148 not racy on the input, 530 real misses, 904 on inputs not checked; compute-sanitizer (any of memcheck / racecheck / synccheck / initcheck): 148 not racy on the input, 530 real misses, 904 on inputs not checked; HiRace: 148 not racy on the input, 0 real misses; iGUARD: 148 not racy on the input, 144 real misses, 32 on inputs not checked; SuperCollider: 2 not racy on the input, 4 real misses. So the FN cells of cuVein (both modes) and HiRace on this suite contain no missed race: on input-level truth their recall is 100% and the label-based ratio under-states it. The label-based cells are kept as pre-registered.

### HiRace artifact Table 1, reproduced verbatim (`make table1`)

The artifact's driver (`scripts/hirace_experiments.py`, unmodified): every IndigoSuite code × 6 graphs, 256 threads/block × 1024 blocks, one run each, 300 s timeout, tools = HiRace (hand-instrumented twin), iGUARD, Compute Sanitizer racecheck, and the uninstrumented run's sequential comparison. Predicates are the artifact's (`gen_table1.py`): *found* = reports>0 on a code that is not `boundsBug`; *missed* = 0 reports on a `Bug` code that is not `boundsBug`. Because *found* also counts bug-free codes, the last columns split it: found-on-racy (TP) and flagged-bug-free (FP). The `paper` rows are the published Table I (`published/hirace_table1.csv`, transcribed from the artifact's `results/paper_figures/table1.png`), not measured here.

Cross-check of the two independent HiRace runs (our per-row runner, 3 reps at -O3 sm_89, vs the artifact driver, 1 run at nvcc defaults): **3540/3540** (code, graph) verdicts agree.

### cuVein at two operating points (D2)

Race u Latent = the program verdict the harness records (a Latent report counts, as it always did). Race alone = only reports that raced in the recorded run (vector-clock: `structural`/`model_bug`; scalar-clock cannot tell Race from Latent, so there the two points coincide). `latent` / `sc` = programs with at least one Latent report / unordered strong conflict (SC, never a RACE; D12), counted as neither TP nor FP. FP/TP as in the accuracy table (denominators exclude ERROR/TIMEOUT); `n/a` = rows analysed before T9 (no class note), excluded from the Race-alone counts. `a2` (T14, `design/a2_flag.md`) = programs whose positive at that point rests only on reports every DR instance of which a window-consistent coherence order could have ordered (A2 not assumed), as FP / TP by label: counted there and as neither TP nor FP in the point's own column; only rows whose dumps carry the flag. `model_bug` = programs with a report R1 certifies and HbClock saw racing (an annotation on the report's verdict, informational: the verdict is its class's, so an SC report with it is a Strong conflict).

### cuVein false positives by report class and root cause

A program counts as FP above on ANY RACE verdict. `structural-FP` = programs with >=1 report HbClock observed racing (structural/model_bug); the rest carry only `latent` reports (no dynamic race, no static proof). Causes are per program as the SET of its reports' causes (see `eval/FP_DIAGNOSIS.md`): RC1 cuda::atomic load/store not modelled, RC2 latent on barrier/lock idioms, RC3 pair mis-attribution, RC4 same-pc idempotent write, RC5 ScoR volatile handshake.

## 4. Overhead (slowdown vs native, same binary+input)

Ratio = tool wall / native wall of the same program (median of reps). TIMEOUT/ERROR runs are excluded (their true slowdown exceeds the cap), so the cuVein figures are lower bounds. sanitizer rows use the native wall measured by the cuVein/iGUARD runners for the same id. SuperCollider is timed against the artifact's own uninstrumented binary, both inside the same Singularity container, so ~0.3 s of container start-up sits in numerator and denominator and compresses its ratio towards 1 on sub-second programs.

## 4a. Overhead per detector per test suite (min / max / avg / mid)

Slowdown = tool wall / native wall of the same program and input (median of reps); SuperCollider is measured against its own uninstrumented binary in the same container. Cell = `min / max / avg / mid (geomean), n` where avg is the arithmetic mean, mid the median (middle value over the finished programs) and n the number of programs the detector finished (TIMEOUT/ERROR runs are excluded, so heavy suites under-state the true cost: see TO in §2c). The geomean is given because the mean of ratios is dominated by a few outliers. `-` = no finished program / tool not run. The compute-sanitizer(any) column is the slowest of its four tools per program.

## 4b. Memory footprint (peak RSS of the whole process tree)

Peak RSS = max over a program's reps of the accelprof process tree's resident set (0.1 s `/proc` poller; runs shorter than a poll interval are under-sampled, which is why a few tiny programs sit below the floor). Cells are `min / median / geomean / max` in MB over the programs that finished (RACE/CLEAN); `× floor` is the median over the Compute-Sanitizer floor, the median peak of the ScoR litmus programs (baselines harness: 852 MB, P5; E-series driver: 818 MB, E5; `eval/REPORT.md` quotes ~818 MB). `unfinished` = TIMEOUT/ERROR programs with the last RSS observed before the kill — a lower bound of what they need. Native RSS is not recorded by either harness (the native runs are timed, not polled).

## 5. Pre-registered expectations (computed)

- **X1: PARTIAL** — cuVein vector-clock P1 default: **0/100 race-free programs reported RACE (0%)**, 100/100 racy caught (0 err/timeout excluded). iGUARD on P1 (both builds): 100/200 race-free reported RACE, 196/200 racy caught (0 err/timeout). Expectation was 'cuVein reports most'.
- **X2: CONFIRMED** — cuVein vector-clock P1 slower_atomic: **0/100 race-free reported RACE (0%)** vs 0/100 on default. Expectation was ~0; met.
- **X3: CONFIRMED** — HiRace (Indigo original suite, bug-free codes x 7 inputs): **0 FP / 1260 race-free -> 0-FP claim HOLDS**, 1714/1862 racy caught. cuVein vector-clock PI: 0/1260 race-free reported RACE, 1714/1862 racy caught. iGUARD PI: 634/1260 race-free reported RACE, 1538/1862 racy caught.
- **X4: CONFIRMED** — P3 race-free graph codes: cuVein vector-clock **16/60 reported RACE** (over-reports, matches REPORT.md F5); iGUARD 48/60 reported RACE; HiRace 0/1260 on its race-free patterns.
- **X5: RECORDED** — P4 reduction volatile-tail vs RACEY missing-fence per build in the P4 table (record-only). See P4 rows.
- **X6: CONFIRMED** — canary: cuVein vector-clock=RACE, cuVein scalar-clock=CLEAN (expected RACE / not-RACE); iGUARD=CLEAN (the canary's contested words are `__device__` globals, outside iGUARD's cuMemAlloc-tracked metadata range).
- **X7: see §4** — geomean slowdown per tool over P1/P7 in the overhead table.

## 6. To re-run after a detector revision

```
bash eval/baselines/setup/run_full.sh      # everything (corpora, all tools)
bash eval/baselines/setup/run_rerun.sh     # cuVein only, after a detector revision
```
`run_rerun.sh` pins the revision (`setup/cuvein_rev.sh` → `cuvein_rev.status` + full diff under `setup/cuvein_rev/`), moves the previous cuVein rows to `eval/results/prefix_<rev>/` (`supersede_prefix.sh`, nothing deleted), re-runs P1–P8 (32 shards) and P9 (20-min cap) in both modes, re-derives the keep/diagnose id lists from the new rows (`mk_followup_ids.py`) and chains keep → diagnose → `p_final2.sh`. Run the smoke gate first (`fpfix_smoke_ids.txt`, both modes).
Submits the whole SLURM chain (corpus build → cuVein sharded run → sanitizer family → iGUARD build+run → HiRace → keep/diagnose → merge/classify/tables) and regenerates every `eval/results/baselines-*.csv` and this file. Individual stages: `mk_manifest.py`, `build_corpora.py`, `build_indigo.py`, `build_indigo2.py`, `parallel.py {run,merge}`, `run_sanitizer.py`, `run_hirace.py`, `run_iguard.py`, `classify_residuals.py`, `classify_fp_causes.py`, `classify_endpoints.py`, `make_tables.py`.
